title: Common AI Penetration-Agent Architecture Patterns (Six Schools)
description: Hierarchical multi-agent, collaborative, intent-driven super-agent, monitored black box, CS-MCP, and human balancing
detail:
Six architecture patterns from a meta-analysis of 17 award-winning teams in past exercises (yzddmr6):
1. Hierarchical multi-agent: a main planner + expert sub-agents (LangGraph/CrewAI) — complex orchestration
2. Collaborative multi-agent: parallel exploration + shared knowledge base
3. Intent-driven super-agent: a single strong model operating autonomously in a sandbox, given only high-level intent (Claude Agent SDK, e.g., tinyctfer)
4. Monitored black box: external asynchronous monitoring of multiple instances
5. Client-server MCP: decoupling the brain from tools
6. Human-in-the-loop dual agent: an executor + an advisor with veto power
Common conclusions: sandboxing is a red line; prompt engineering determines the ceiling (configuration over hardcoding); memory management is a core challenge; a minimal toolset (3-5 core tools) is better than an all-in-one set; do not trust completely (multi-step verification + high-risk review).
Champion trend = intent-driven + parallel workers + verification under incomplete trust.
Source: https://yzddmr6.com/posts/manus-pentest-report
